title: Recognising KPT in T-plurals
summary: Notice the weak consonant grade before the final plural -t.
objectives: Separate the final plural -t from the noun stem.
Prepare to produce familiar KPT plurals.

sections.title: Stem first, plural ending second
paragraphs: Some familiar nouns use a weak consonant grade before plural -t.
Identify the stem change separately from the final -t.

sections.title: Known pairs only
paragraphs: This pack teaches the displayed word pairs from first principles.
Do not assume every unfamiliar noun changes in the same way.

commonMistakes: Do not attach -t to the unchanged strong form when the learned pair uses KPT.
Do not count an internal t as the plural ending.
Do not guess beyond the displayed vocabulary.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Is keitto singular or plural?
practiceExercises.explanation: keitto is singular. The singular is keitto (“soup”); the T-plural is keitot (“soups”). The plural also shows tt → t.

optionFeedback.singular: Correct. keitto is singular. The singular is keitto (“soup”); the T-plural is keitot (“soups”). The plural also shows tt → t.
optionFeedback.plural: keitto is not plural in this pair. keitto is singular. The singular is keitto (“soup”); the T-plural is keitot (“soups”). The plural also shows tt → t.
